nodes.title: The inert Gross CM datum
nodes.statement: An inert CM datum is the tuple in the standing hypotheses, with the actual Hecke character, Gross CM curve, rank-one avatar lattice, embeddings and differential/period comparison. It also records the chosen p-adic place of H. This is input data on imported carriers, not a new CM-curve or Hecke-character theory. Coefficient extension R→R′ transports T by tensor product, W by the induced discrete quotient, and Λ_R by completed scalar extension.
hypotheses: p≥5 is prime and inert in the imaginary quadratic field K; p does not divide h_K. H is the Hilbert class field.

nodes.title: Specialization dimension is bounded by the local length

hypotheses: A is a commutative local ring; M is arbitrary (both sides may be infinite).
In the application X is finitely generated and torsion over Λ_R=R[[Γ⁻]], and ρ is a finite character of Γ⁻ with values in a finite extension Lρ of L.
proofSteps: κ⊗_A M is an A-module quotient of M, so its A-length is at most that of M (Module.length_le_of_surjective).
The A-length of a κ-vector space equals its κ-length (IsLocalRing.length_restrictScalars with B=κ, residue degree one), which is its κ-dimension (Module.length_eq_finrank).

Λ_R is a two-dimensional regular local ring, so its localization at the height-one prime P is a discrete valuation ring with residue field Frac(Λ_R/P)=L(ρ), and X⊗κ(P) is the specialization X⊗_(Λ_R,ρ)L(ρ).

The length of X_P is the coefficient of P in the characteristic divisor (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4; TauCetiRoadmap README §4.6, charDivisor). P is generated by the minimal polynomial of ρ(γ)−1 over L, which has simple roots, so this coefficient is the order of vanishing at ρ(γ)−1 of a generator of char(X).

If f is a unit multiple of an element with coefficients in O, an automorphism of Φ(μ_(p^r)) over Φ sends ρ(γ) to ρ(γ)⁻¹, because Φ/Q_p is unramified, and it fixes the coefficients of f; hence ord_ρ f=ord_(ρ⁻¹) f.

X=Λ_R/(g²), with g the minimal polynomial of ρ(γ)−1, has specialization dimension one and ord_ρ char(X)=2.
